  2. Lighting is key, you probably don't have a lighting kit, and most people feel awkward taking selfies in public like I'll describe so make sure you have an open window in your house on a sunny day. The house should be clean, and the view shouldn't be of your neighbors siding if possible. If you have a camera and a tripod, set your camera on some sort of timed burst mode and go crazy, or just set it on a counter at about chest to eye height. Take goofy shots, pretend you're a model and over pose, caress the wall, look at the camera like you're a ham in starvation mode and it's ice cold Beetus. Now that you have the weird part of you all out of your system, take some laughing at yourself for being a dunce, a couple relaxed, some looking away at the wall laughing, and maybe some more less over the top model poses now that you're in your photo taking zen. Look at the camera, away from the camera, above and below. Review and see what poses looked the best, then go back and do it again. You may have to take hundreds and hundreds of shots before you find 'the one' because we are so much more critical of ourselves we notice every flaw in every picture. Some cameras have remotes that you can use so you don't have to go back and forth to get another set of shots going. There is also a rule of thirds, there are tons of portrait photography instructional videos on youtube, try changing the search terms from "how to look good in pictures" to "portrait photography in natural lighting" or something like that, you'll see how they compose the shot, and how they post the model.

If your camera can connect to your computer for a live view of shots, that can also be helpful, it's like looking in the mirror and taking the perfect picture.
